133	
134	If a page needs to show something closer to real code shape and flow, prefer a config file excerpt or a shell session instead — most of what this wiki documents is easier to show that way, and it keeps this style guide's own promise that code blocks stay short and skimmable.

154

156	
157	**Step 1. Check the current branch.**

162	```
163

169	sqlite> .headers on
170	sqlite> .show

172	     headers: on
173	        mode: column

175	```
176

178	
179	```diff

181	-cache_seconds = 30
182	+cache_seconds = 120
183	```

195	*Owner: Theo Bram*

**Step 1. Check the current branch.**

```bash
$ git status --short --branch
## docs-style-cleanup...origin/docs-style-cleanup
```

**Step 2. Open the sample database used in this walk-through.**

```text
$ sqlite3 sample.db
sqlite> .mode column
sqlite> .headers on
sqlite> .show
        echo: off
     headers: on
        mode: column
sqlite> .quit
```

**Step 3. Edit the sample config file and confirm the change.**

```diff
[example]
-cache_seconds = 30
+cache_seconds = 120
```

```bash
$ git diff --stat
 docs/docs-style/assets/code-samples/example.ini | 2 +-
 One file changed: one added, one removed.
```

This three-step shape — command, tool exchange, config change — covers most of what appears elsewhere in the wiki. Observe that each block stays under the 12-line command line ceiling, each uses one tag consistently, and the diff block is the only place `+`/`-` marks appear outside prose.

## Review and Sign-off

*Owner: Theo Bram*

New or changed code blocks get a second look before a page is published, on the same quarterly cycle that governs the rest of the docs-style folder. A reviewer checks for:

* a language tag on every fence
* consistent prompt markers within a single block
* no pasted output that includes a contributor's own working directory or host name
* line counts within the limits set above

Small fixes — a missing tag, a stray tab character — can be made directly during review without a second round. Anything larger, such as reworking a whole worked example, goes back to the page's own owner first.

## Common Mistakes

1. Pasting an entire multi-screen sqlite3 session when three lines would show the same point.
2. Mixing `$` and no-prompt lines within the same shell block, so a reader cannot tell where the command ends and the output begins.
3. Using a Python-shaped code fence tagged `python` for something that is really shell output, just because it happens to contain a colon.
4. Forgetting the trailing output comment on a Python-shaped snippet, leaving a reader to guess what the last line returns.
5. Config excerpts with no tag at all, which fall back to plain rendering and lose the highlighting a reader expects.

## Files and Paths Referenced by This Page

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `docs/docs-style/code-block-standards.md` | This page; the canonical source for fenced block, prompt, and Python-shaped snippet rules |
| `docs/docs-style/markdown-conventions.md` | General Markdown rules this page builds on for fence syntax and inline code spans |
| `docs/docs-style/voice-and-tone.md` | House voice rules referenced for the wording used in output comments |
| `docs/docs-style/terminology-glossary.md` | Canonical wiki-wide term list; this page's glossary section is a local subset of it |
| `docs/docs-style/style-checklist.rst` | Pre-publish checklist; includes a line item covering fenced block tags |
| `docs/docs-style/front-matter-schema.yaml` | Defines the required header fields (title, version, owner, updated date) checked at publish time |
| `docs/docs-style/assets/code-samples/` | Folder holding the copy-pasteable example files referenced in worked examples, including `example.ini` |
| `scripts/check-code-blocks.sh` | Shell script run ahead of a commit that scans changed pages for missing language tags and stray tab characters |
| `docs/_build/` | Generated output folder produced by the site generator; never edited by hand |

## Tools and Libraries

| Tool / Package | Version | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Pygments | 2.18 | Syntax highlighting engine used by the site generator to color fenced blocks |
| MkDocs | 1.6.0 | Static site generator that turns the pages under `docs/` into the published wiki |
| mkdocs-material | 9.5.18 | Theme supplying the copy-button widget and the tag-based color scheme used throughout |
| markdownlint-cli | 0.41.0 | Checks heading order, list style, and fence syntax before a page is published |
| shellcheck | 0.9.0 | Flags shell snippets that would not run cleanly in a plain POSIX shell |
| sqlite3 (CLI) | 3.46.0 | Reference version used when formatting interactive sqlite3 session examples |
| mdformat | 0.7.17 | Normalizes spacing inside fenced blocks ahead of a commit |

| 2025-05-12 | v1.4 | Retired the old triple-caret marker for output in favor of the leading `#` output comment style |
| 2024-12-03 | v1.3 | Added the line-length table and the 100-character wrap width for command line blocks |

| 2024-02-14 | v1.1 | Added the glossary section and cross-linked Markdown Conventions for the first time |
| 2023-10-01 | v1.0 | First published version; covered fenced block language tags and prompt markers only |

TITLE: Contributor Onboarding Notes
VERSION: v1.0.0
OWNER: Field Guides (Owen Petrakis)
LAST UPDATED: 2024-03-22

================================================================================
OVERVIEW
================================================================================

Welcome to the auditlog documentation program. This guide gets you started as a
documentation contributor. You will find information here on our folder layout,
naming conventions, page structures, writing style, and the workflows we use to
review and publish documentation. The docs-style folder is the source of truth
for how we write and maintain documentation across the package.

If you get stuck on something not covered here, reach out to Kara Voss (Docs
Program) or Owen Petrakis (Field Guides). For questions about specific content
areas, check the section owner listed under each heading.

================================================================================
FOLDER LAYOUT AND NAMING CONVENTIONS
================================================================================

Section Owner: Kara Voss

The repository root contains a docs/ folder where all user-facing documentation
lives, and a docs-style/ folder that holds the documentation program guidelines
themselves. The structure is flat within docs-style; we avoid nested folders.

Files in docs-style/ are named with lowercase and hyphens, never underscores:

  • voice-and-tone.md
  • page-templates.md
  • markdown-conventions.md
  • code-block-standards.md
  • review-cadence.md
  • publishing-workflow.md

We keep a single terminology-glossary.md for terms shared across the program.
Each page in docs-style/ includes its own concise glossary section; the shared
glossary is for broader reference and periodic updates.

The docs/ folder contains the main package documentation. Pages there follow
the same lowercase-hyphen naming scheme. Use subdirectories in docs/ only when
a section grows beyond five pages; prefer a flat structure. Common subdirectories:

  - docs/tutorials/
  - docs/how-to-guides/
  - docs/reference/
  - docs/explanations/

Our front matter schema (see front-matter-schema.yaml) requires that every
page include title, version, owner, and last-updated date at the top. The schema
is YAML and strict; if you deviate, the publishing workflow will flag it during
validation.

================================================================================
PAGE FORMAT AND TEMPLATES
================================================================================

Section Owner: Kara Voss

All pages must follow the structure and metadata rules defined in page-
templates.md. That page provides complete templates for tutorials, how-to
guides, reference material, and explanations. Use the templates exactly as
provided; do not invent new page types.

Key rules:
  - Every page opens with a YAML front matter block containing title, version,
    owner, and last-updated date.
  - Markdown is the standard format for user-facing docs (docs/ folder).
  - Configuration and meta-documentation in docs-style/ may use .txt, .md, or
    .rst formats. Be consistent within the file type.
  - Headings use ATX-style (# ## ###, etc.) in Markdown; reStructuredText pages
    use overlines and underlines.
  - Code blocks should follow code-block-standards.md exactly.
  - Always include a Related Pages section that links to sibling pages.

When you create a new page, copy the relevant template from page-templates.md
and fill in the required sections. Do not skip sections, even if they seem
optional. Completeness is a quality standard in our program.

================================================================================
WRITING STYLE AND VOICE
================================================================================

Section Owner: Kara Voss

Read voice-and-tone.md in full before you write. It defines our brand voice as
clear, direct, and jargon-aware. We write for people with varying expertise
levels; explain terms the first time you use them, and link to the glossary.

Specific guidance:

  1. Use second person (you, your) when giving instructions. "Run the service"
     is better than "The service is run" or "One should run the service."

  2. Use imperative mood for procedures. "Open the configuration file" instead
     of "You should open the configuration file."

  3. Avoid vague language. "In some cases" or "depending on the situation" is
     weak. Be specific: "If the database file is corrupt, the service will not
     start."

  4. Write in active voice. Passive voice is acceptable when the actor is
     unknown or irrelevant.

  5. Capitalize product and tool names consistently. See the terminology
     glossary for proper capitalization of internal names.

  6. Keep paragraphs short (3–5 sentences). Break up dense content with headings
     and lists.

  7. Use the Oxford comma (a, b, and c).

The markdown-conventions.md page covers specific formatting for emphasis,
links, headings, and lists. Review it when you are unsure about punctuation or
structure within Markdown.

================================================================================
TERMINOLOGY AND GLOSSARY UPKEEP
================================================================================

Section Owner: Mara Olsen

The shared terminology-glossary.md page is the single source of truth for
terms used across the documentation program. If you define a term in your own
page, check the glossary first to see if it is already documented.

When should you add a new term?

  • The term is used across multiple pages or multiple sections within a page.
  • The term is specific to the package or this documentation program (e.g.,
    "loopback HTTP service," "database file").
  • The term might be unfamiliar to someone new to the team.

How to add a term:

  1. Propose the term and definition on a branch. Open a pull request to
     terminology-glossary.md.

  2. Link to that PR in your own page so reviewers see both together.

  3. Once the term is merged, update your page to reference the glossary
     entry, not duplicate the definition.

Each page may have its own brief glossary section for terms used only within
that page. Do not duplicate the shared glossary in every page's local glossary.

The glossary-terms.txt worksheet is a scratchpad used during authoring. List
new or uncertain terms there as you write, then reconcile them with the main
glossary during review. This worksheet is not published; it is internal only.

================================================================================
REVIEW PROCESS AND CADENCE
================================================================================

Section Owner: Theo Bram

Documentation review follows the schedule and rules in review-cadence.md. In
summary:

  • New pages enter the "Early Review" stage before being finalized. Reviewers
    check for clarity, completeness, and alignment with our standards.

  • All changes to docs-style/ (program documentation) are reviewed by at least
    two members of the Docs Program team. Owen Petrakis and Kara Voss typically
    hold this responsibility.

  • Changes to user-facing documentation in docs/ are reviewed by one domain
    expert (the feature owner or subject matter expert) and one member of the
    Docs Program team.

  • The review window is 3–5 business days for routine changes and 5–7 days for
    significant new content.

  • If a reviewer requests changes, you have 2 business days to respond. After
    that period, the item may be bumped to the next review cycle.

Use the review-cadence.md page as your reference for exact SLAs and the review
rubric. It also lists who is responsible for each area.

================================================================================
PUBLISHING WORKFLOW AND VALIDATION
================================================================================

Section Owner: Mara Olsen

The publishing-workflow.md page walks through how documentation moves from your
branch to the live site. The process is semi-automated:

  1. You push your branch to the repository.

  2. A pre-commit hook validates your front matter against front-matter-
     schema.yaml. If validation fails, your commit is blocked and you must fix
     the YAML.

  3. You open a pull request and request review from the appropriate team (see
     review-cadence.md).

  4. Once validated, you merge to main. Do not merge without validation.

  5. On merge, a CI job runs markdown lint (against markdown-conventions.md),
     code-block validation (against code-block-standards.md), and a link
     checker. If any check fails, the merge is rolled back. You must fix issues
     and reopen the PR.

  6. After CI passes, the documentation is automatically published to the live
     site within 30 minutes. Check the live site to confirm your changes appear
     as expected.

Some pages (changelogs, glossaries, and reference material) are published more
frequently; see publishing-workflow.md for details. If you are writing a page
that will be updated often, ask Mara Olsen before merging so we can set up
custom publishing rules.

================================================================================
TOOLS AND DEPENDENCIES
================================================================================

The documentation program uses the following tools and libraries:

┌─────────────────────┬───────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Tool / Library      │ Version   │ Purpose                              │
├─────────────────────┼───────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Python              │ 3.9       │ Markdown validator and front matter  │
│                     │           │ schema checker                       │
├─────────────────────┼───────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Markdown            │ 3.4.1     │ Markdown parsing and validation      │
├─────────────────────┼───────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤
│ yamllint            │ 1.26.3    │ YAML linting for front matter        │
├─────────────────────┼───────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Sphinx              │ 5.0       │ Documentation build and site         │
│                     │           │ generation                           │
├─────────────────────┼───────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤
│ linkchecker         │ 10.2.1    │ Broken link detection                │
├─────────────────────┼───────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤
│ GitHub Actions      │ (service) │ CI/CD pipeline for validation and    │
│                     │           │ publishing                           │
└─────────────────────┴───────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┘

The scripts/ folder contains helper scripts for common tasks:

  • scripts/validate-docs.py — runs all validators locally before pushing
  • scripts/term-checker.py — checks for undefined terms in a page
  • scripts/update-frontmatter.py — updates version and date fields in bulk
  • scripts/build-local.sh — builds the documentation site locally for preview

Run validate-docs.py before you commit. It catches most errors and saves time
in review.

================================================================================
REPOSITORY FILES AND PATHS
================================================================================

Below are the key files and folders referenced in this guide:

FILE / PATH                                    PURPOSE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

                                               folder and program governance

                                               from branch to live site

                                               language labeling

                                               tools

                                               (title, version, owner, etc.)

docs-style/changelog-notes.rst                 Format for writing changelog
                                               entries

                                               published)

docs/                                          Root folder for all user-facing
                                               documentation

                                               glossary terms

                                               for preview

================================================================================
TERMINOLOGY AND GLOSSARY
================================================================================

Attribute Block
  The YAML front matter section at the top of a page containing title, version,
  owner, and last-updated date. Required on all pages. See front-matter-
  schema.yaml for the exact schema.

Domain Expert
  A team member responsible for a feature or area of the package. They are one
  of the two required reviewers for pages in their domain.

Docs Program
  The team responsible for documentation standards and tooling. Members include
  Kara Voss, Priya Nair, and Owen Petrakis. They review all changes to docs-
  style/ and maintain voice and tone standards.

Early Review
  The initial review stage for new pages, before they are considered complete.
  Reviewers check clarity, structure, and alignment with guidelines.

Front Matter
  The metadata block at the top of a page, written in YAML. Includes title,
  version, owner, and date.

Local Glossary
  A glossary section within a single page that defines terms used only within
  that page. Different from the shared terminology-glossary.md.

Page Owner
  The person primarily responsible for a page's accuracy and updates. Listed in
  the page's front matter.

Shared Glossary
  The single terminology-glossary.md file that defines terms used across
  multiple pages or the entire documentation program. The source of truth for
  term definitions.

Template
  A standard structure for a given page type (tutorial, how-to, reference,
  explanation). Found in page-templates.md. All pages must follow a template.

Voice and Tone
  The style and personality of the documentation. Defined in voice-and-tone.md
  as clear, direct, and jargon-aware.

1	# ============================================================================
2	# docs-style/front-matter-schema.yaml
3	# ============================================================================
4	# This file is itself a documentation page. Its own header block sits
5	# directly below, in the same shape that every other auditlog documentation
6	# file — Markdown, RST, or plain text — must reproduce at the top of the
7	# file, whether as literal YAML between --- markers or as a short field list
8	# near the top of the page.
9	# ============================================================================
10	
11	---
12	title: Front Matter Schema
13	version: "1.4"
14	owner: Field Guides (Owen Petrakis)
15	last_updated: 2026-04-01
16	summary: >
17	  Specifies the required front matter fields, such as title and owner, that
18	  every auditlog documentation file must include at the top.
19	---
20	
21	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
22	# 1. Purpose and Coverage
23	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
24	purpose_and_coverage: |
25	  This page defines the fields that must sit at the top of every page in
26	  the auditlog documentation set, and the rules for filling each one in.
27	  "Front matter" here means the small block of key-value fields at the very
28	  top of a file — title, version, owner, last-updated date, and a short
29	  summary — regardless of whether the file is a Markdown page under
30	  docs/docs-style/, a reStructuredText page such as style-checklist.rst, or
31	  a plain text worksheet such as glossary-terms.txt.
32	
33	  The schema exists because the docs-style folder has grown past a dozen
34	  files maintained by three different teams (Docs Program, Platform Tools,
35	  Support Enablement, and Field Guides), and a reader who opens any one of
36	  them should be able to tell at a glance who owns it, how current it is,
37	  and what it is for, without reading past the first few lines.
38	
39	  This page does not tell you how to write the body of a page — that is
40	  covered by voice-and-tone.md and markdown-conventions.md — and it does
41	  not tell you which template to start a new page from — that is
42	  page-templates.md. It only defines the header block that sits above all
43	  of that, and the small amount of process around keeping it current.
44	
45	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
46	# 2. Required Fields
47	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
48	# Section owner: Field Guides (Owen Petrakis)
49	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
50	required_fields:
51	  - name: title
52	    type: string
53	    required: true
54	    description: >
55	      The page's display name, written in title case for Markdown and RST
56	      pages, and matched exactly wherever another page links to it (see
57	      Related Pages, below). Do not shorten it in the header and then use
58	      a longer form in a link, or the other way round.
59	    example: "Front Matter Schema"
60	
61	  - name: version
62	    type: string
63	    required: true
64	    description: >
65	      A plain version marker for the page, not the package. Most pages in
66	      this folder use a bare decimal such as 1.4; a few use a semantic
67	      "v" prefix such as v1.2.0. Either is acceptable on an existing page,
68	      but new pages should default to the bare decimal form (1.0, 1.1,
69	      1.2, and so on) unless the owning team already uses the prefixed
70	      form for that page.
71	    example: "1.4"
72	
73	  - name: owner
74	    type: string
75	    required: true
76	    description: >
77	      Team name followed by a person's name in parentheses, for example
78	      "Field Guides (Owen Petrakis)". Some older pages reverse this to
79	      "Owen Petrakis (Field Guides)" — both forms parse fine for a human
80	      reader, but new pages should put the team first, since that is what
81	      most of the folder already does.
82	    example: "Docs Program (Kara Voss)"
83	
84	  - name: last_updated
85	    type: date
86	    required: true
87	    description: >
88	      An ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) marking the day the page's content
89	      was last substantively changed — not the day someone fixed a typo
90	      or reflowed a paragraph. The field name itself appears as
91	      "last-updated" in Markdown and RST headers and as last_updated in
92	      this file; both spellings are fine, just be consistent within a
93	      single page.
94	    example: "2026-04-01"
95	
96	  - name: summary
97	    type: string
98	    required: true
99	    description: >
100	      One to two sentences describing what the page covers, written so
101	      that it can stand alone in a folder listing or a search result.
102	      Avoid restating the title; say what a reader will get from the
103	      page instead.
104	    example: >
105	      Specifies the required front matter fields, such as title and
106	      owner, that every auditlog documentation file must include at
107	      the top.
108	
109	optional_fields:
110	  - name: status
111	    type: string
112	    required: false
113	    description: >
114	      One of draft, current, or closed. Pages without this field are
115	      assumed current. Use draft while a page is still being shaped and
116	      closed once a page has been folded into another and is being kept
117	      only for its links.
118	    example: "current"
119	
120	  - name: section_owners
121	    type: list
122	    required: false
123	    description: >
124	      An optional list naming which team owns which section, for pages
125	      long enough that a single page-level owner doesn't tell the whole
126	      story. When used, each section heading in the body should carry a
127	      short "Section owner:" line that matches an entry here.
128	    example: "[Docs Program (Kara Voss), Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)]"
129	
130	  - name: tags
131	    type: list
132	    required: false
133	    description: >
134	      Free-text labels used loosely for search, such as [style, glossary,
135	      publishing]. Not validated against a fixed list at this time.
136	    example: "[schema, front-matter, docs-style]"
137	
138	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
139	# 3. Field Definitions in Depth
140	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
141	field_definitions_in_depth: |
142	  Title. The title is what shows up in the Related Pages section of every
143	  other page that links to yours, so treat a change to it as a small
144	  cross-folder change: search the folder for the old title before you
145	  commit the new one, since links point to titles as much as to file
146	  paths. A quick way to find stale references is a plain text search
147	  across the folder for the exact old title string.
148	
149	  Version. Bump the version whenever the body of the page changes in a
150	  way a returning reader would want to know about — a new required field,
151	  a changed procedure, a corrected example. Do not bump the version for
152	  whitespace or spelling fixes; note those only in the change log if you
153	  keep one on the page, or skip them entirely for very small fixes. There
154	  is ongoing disagreement in the folder about whether the version should
155	  be a bare decimal or a three-part semantic version; both schemes are in
156	  live use as of this writing and this page does not attempt to settle it.
157	
158	  Owner. One team and one named person, always. Do not list two teams in
159	  the owner field — use section_owners for that instead, described above.
160	  When ownership moves from one person to another, update the owner field
161	  on the same day you hand off the page, not on the day the handoff was
162	  discussed. A page whose owner field names someone who has moved to a
163	  different team should be treated as stale even if the page's content is
164	  still accurate.
165	
166	  Last-updated date. This date is the one the review cadence process
167	  reads to decide whether a page is due for another look — see
168	  review-cadence.md for the schedule itself. Set it only when you change
169	  the page's content, not when you open it to read, and not when an
170	  automated pass reformats spacing or fixes a broken link without
171	  touching the meaning of the text.
172	
173	  Summary. Keep it to one or two sentences. A summary that runs to a full
174	  paragraph is a sign the page is trying to cover more than one topic and
175	  might be a candidate for splitting — raise that with the page's owner
176	  rather than just trimming the summary to fit.
177	
178	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
179	# 4. Voice and Front Matter
180	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
181	# Section owner: Docs Program (Kara Voss)
182	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
183	voice_and_front_matter: |
184	  The header block is the one part of a page where terse, fragment-style
185	  writing is expected rather than the fuller sentences voice-and-tone.md
186	  asks for in the body. Field values should read like labels, not like
187	  sentences: "Specifies the required front matter fields..." rather than
188	  "This page specifies the required front matter fields...". The Voice
189	  and Tone Guide covers body prose in detail; this schema only asks that
190	  summary fields stay short enough to fit on one line in a folder
191	  listing, roughly 20 words or fewer.
192	
193	  Capitalization of field labels in a rendered header is not strictly
194	  fixed across the folder — some pages show "Last Updated," others "Last
195	  updated," and a couple of older pages still show "Updated." Pick one
196	  form per page and hold it for every field on that page; do not mix
197	  "Owner" and "owner" in the same header block.
198	
199	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
200	# 5. Page Template Integration
201	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
202	# Section owner: Docs Program (Kara Voss)
203	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
204	page_template_integration: |
205	  page-templates.md, currently at version 1.3, ships one starter file for
206	  each of the three page shapes used in this folder — a short reference
207	  page, a longer procedure page, and a worksheet-style page — and every
208	  one of those starters already has the five required fields filled in
209	  with stand-in-shaped values (a bracketed title, a bracketed owner,
210	  and so on) so a writer only has to replace them, not remember which
211	  fields exist.
212	
213	  When this schema changes — for example, the 1.4 update below that adds
214	  the related-pages and tools-table requirements to every page, not just
215	  procedure pages — the templates need a matching update so new pages
216	  don't get created against a stale shape. That update is tracked as a
217	  small, separate item on page-templates.md's own change log, not on this
218	  one.
219	
220	  A minimal starter header, copied from the reference-page template,
221	  looks like this before anyone fills it in:
222	
223	  ---
224	  title: [Page Title]
225	  version: 1.0
226	  owner: [Team Name] ([Person Name])
227	  last_updated: [YYYY-MM-DD]
228	  summary: >
229	    [One to two sentences describing what this page covers.]
230	  ---
231	
232	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
233	# 6. Glossary Upkeep
234	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
235	# Section owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)
236	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
237	glossary_upkeep: |
238	  Every page's terminology section, described further under Terminology
239	  below, is expected to define terms in a way that does not contradict
240	  terminology-glossary.md, the folder's shared glossary. Front matter
241	  itself does not carry glossary entries directly, but the summary field
242	  is the one place a term from the glossary is most likely to appear in a
243	  sentence a reader sees before opening the page, so it is worth checking
244	  new or changed summaries against the glossary during a page's review.
245	
246	  The upkeep procedure is short:
247	
248	  1. When a page's terminology section adds a term the shared glossary
249	     does not yet have, open a short entry in terminology-glossary.md in
250	     the same change, rather than leaving the term defined only on the
251	     one page that introduced it.
252	  2. When a page's terminology section defines an existing glossary term
253	     differently than the glossary does, fix the page to match the
254	     glossary rather than the other way round — the glossary is the
255	     source every other page is expected to agree with.
256	  3. Once a quarter, someone from Platform Tools skims every terminology
257	     section in the folder against the glossary and flags drift. The
258	     glossary itself was last rebuilt in a pass that finished in April
259	     2026, and the schema page you're reading now was checked against
260	     that pass.
261	
262	  glossary-terms.txt is a separate, older worksheet kept for draft terms
263	  that have not yet been promoted into terminology-glossary.md proper —
264	  treat anything listed there as unsettled, not as a page you can cite.
265	
266	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
267	# 7. Review Cadence Integration
268	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
269	# Section owner: Docs Program (Kara Voss)
270	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
271	review_cadence_integration: |
272	  The last-updated field is the single piece of front matter the review
273	  cadence process depends on most directly: review-cadence.md sorts every
274	  page in the folder by that date and flags anything older than the
275	  window set for its page type. A page whose owner field names someone no
276	  longer on the relevant team is flagged the same way, even if the date
277	  itself is recent, since a stale owner usually means the review didn't
278	  actually happen even though someone bumped the date.
279	
280	  Because of that, do not "update" the last-updated date on a page
281	  without also making a real content change — a date-only bump defeats
282	  the purpose of the cadence check and hides pages that genuinely need a
283	  look. If a review confirms a page is still accurate with no changes
284	  needed, note that in the page's own change log (see below) as a
285	  no-change entry rather than editing the date on its own.
286	
287	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
288	# 8. Docs Publishing Workflow Integration
289	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
290	# Section owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)
291	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
292	publishing_workflow_integration: |
293	  publishing-workflow.md describes the full path from a merged change to
294	  a published page; the piece that belongs on this page is the one step
295	  where front matter is checked before anything else runs. A short shell
296	  script under scripts/ reads every file changed in a commit, confirms
297	  the five required fields are present and non-empty, and fails the
298	  commit hook if any are missing. It does not check field values for
299	  correctness beyond that — a version of "banana" would still pass — it
300	  only confirms the fields exist.
301	
302	  A typical local run, checking a single changed file before pushing,
303	  looks like this:
304	
305	  $ scripts/check-front-matter.sh docs/docs-style/front-matter-schema.yaml
306	  OK: title, version, owner, last_updated, summary all present
307	
308	  And a pre-commit hook that runs the same check across every staged
309	  Markdown, RST, and YAML file under docs/docs-style/ before allowing a
310	  commit:
311	
312	  #!/usr/bin/env sh
313	  # .git/hooks/pre-commit
314	  changed=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM -- 'docs/docs-style/*.md' 'docs/docs-style/*.rst' 'docs/docs-style/*.yaml')
315	  for f in $changed; do
316	    scripts/check-front-matter.sh "$f" || exit 1
317	  done
318	
319	  A grep-based spot check, useful when the shell script isn't handy, just
320	  confirms the field labels are present somewhere near the top of a file:
321	
322	  $ head -n 12 docs/docs-style/front-matter-schema.yaml | grep -E 'title|version|owner|last_updated|summary'
323	
324	  On Windows, the equivalent using PowerShell's Select-String is:
325	
326	  PS> Get-Content docs\docs-style\front-matter-schema.yaml -TotalCount 12 | Select-String 'title|version|owner|last_updated|summary'
327	
328	  Publishing itself is out of coverage for this page — see
329	  publishing-workflow.md for how a passing check turns into a page on the
330	  published site.
331	
332	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
333	# 9. Worked Examples
334	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
335	worked_examples: |
336	  A complete, valid header for a new procedure page:
337	
338	  ---
339	  title: Glossary Upkeep Checklist
340	  version: 1.0
341	  owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)
342	  last_updated: 2026-06-01
343	  summary: >
344	    Walks through the quarterly pass that checks page terminology
345	    sections against the shared glossary.
346	  ---
347	
348	  A header with three common problems, shown as it might actually get
349	  submitted:
350	
351	  ---
352	  Title: Glossary Upkeep Checklist
353	  version: v1
354	  last_updated: June 1st, 2026
355	  Summary: A checklist.
356	  ---
357	
358	  The problems, in the order a reviewer would flag them:
359	
360	  - The owner field is missing entirely — the check script would fail
361	    the commit on this one alone.
362	  - last_updated is not in ISO 8601 form; "June 1st, 2026" does not sort
363	    correctly against the rest of the folder and the cadence process
364	    cannot parse it.
365	  - The summary is too short to be useful in a folder listing, and field
366	    capitalization ("Title", "Summary") is inconsistent with the rest of
367	    the header ("version", "last_updated").
368	
369	  The fix keeps the same content but corrects the shape:
370	
371	  ---
372	  title: Glossary Upkeep Checklist
373	  version: 1.0
374	  owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)
375	  last_updated: 2026-06-01
376	  summary: >
377	    Walks through the quarterly pass that checks page terminology
378	    sections against the shared glossary.
379	  ---
380	
381	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
382	# 10. Validation Procedure
383	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
384	validation_procedure:
385	  - step: 1
386	    action: >

# ============================================================================
# docs-style/front-matter-schema.yaml
# ============================================================================
# This file is itself a documentation page. Its own header block sits
# directly below, in the same shape that every other auditlog documentation
# file — Markdown, RST, or plain text — must reproduce at the top of the
# file, whether as literal YAML between --- markers or as a short field list
# near the top of the page.
# ============================================================================

---
title: Front Matter Schema
version: "1.4"
owner: Field Guides (Owen Petrakis)
last_updated: 2026-04-01
summary: >
  Specifies the required front matter fields, such as title and owner, that
  every auditlog documentation file must include at the top.
---

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Purpose and Coverage
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
purpose_and_coverage: |
  This page defines the fields that must sit at the top of every page in
  the auditlog documentation set, and the rules for filling each one in.
  "Front matter" here means the small block of key-value fields at the very
  top of a file — title, version, owner, last-updated date, and a short
  summary — regardless of whether the file is a Markdown page under
  docs/docs-style/, a reStructuredText page such as style-checklist.rst, or
  a plain text worksheet such as glossary-terms.txt.

  The schema exists because the docs-style folder has grown past a dozen
  files maintained by three different teams (Docs Program, Platform Tools,
  Support Enablement, and Field Guides), and a reader who opens any one of
  them should be able to tell at a glance who owns it, how current it is,
  and what it is for, without reading past the first few lines.

  This page does not tell you how to write the body of a page — that is
  covered by voice-and-tone.md and markdown-conventions.md — and it does
  not tell you which template to start a new page from — that is
  page-templates.md. It only defines the header block that sits above all
  of that, and the small amount of process around keeping it current.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Required Fields
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section owner: Field Guides (Owen Petrakis)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
required_fields:
  - name: title
    type: string
    required: true
    description: >
      The page's display name, written in title case for Markdown and RST
      pages, and matched exactly wherever another page links to it (see
      Related Pages, below). Do not shorten it in the header and then use
      a longer form in a link, or the other way round.
    example: "Front Matter Schema"

  - name: version
    type: string
    required: true
    description: >
      A plain version marker for the page, not the package. Most pages in
      this folder use a bare decimal such as 1.4; a few use a semantic
      "v" prefix such as v1.2.0. Either is acceptable on an existing page,
      but new pages should default to the bare decimal form (1.0, 1.1,
      1.2, and so on) unless the owning team already uses the prefixed
      form for that page.
    example: "1.4"

  - name: owner
    type: string
    required: true
    description: >
      Team name followed by a person's name in parentheses, for example
      "Field Guides (Owen Petrakis)". Some older pages reverse this to
      "Owen Petrakis (Field Guides)" — both forms parse fine for a human
      reader, but new pages should put the team first, since that is what
      most of the folder already does.
    example: "Docs Program (Kara Voss)"

  - name: last_updated
    type: date
    required: true
    description: >
      An ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) marking the day the page's content
      was last substantively changed — not the day someone fixed a typo
      or reflowed a paragraph. The field name itself appears as
      "last-updated" in Markdown and RST headers and as last_updated in
      this file; both spellings are fine, just be consistent within a
      single page.
    example: "2026-04-01"

  - name: summary
    type: string
    required: true
    description: >
      One to two sentences describing what the page covers, written so
      that it can stand alone in a folder listing or a search result.
      Avoid restating the title; say what a reader will get from the
      page instead.
    example: >
      Specifies the required front matter fields, such as title and
      owner, that every auditlog documentation file must include at
      the top.

optional_fields:
  - name: status
    type: string
    required: false
    description: >
      One of draft, current, or closed. Pages without this field are
      assumed current. Use draft while a page is still being shaped and
      closed once a page has been folded into another and is being kept
      only for its links.
    example: "current"

  - name: section_owners
    type: list
    required: false
    description: >
      An optional list naming which team owns which section, for pages
      long enough that a single page-level owner doesn't tell the whole
      story. When used, each section heading in the body should carry a
      short "Section owner:" line that matches an entry here.
    example: "[Docs Program (Kara Voss), Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)]"

  - name: tags
    type: list
    required: false
    description: >
      Free-text labels used loosely for search, such as [style, glossary,
      publishing]. Not validated against a fixed list at this time.
    example: "[schema, front-matter, docs-style]"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Field Definitions in Depth
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
field_definitions_in_depth: |
  Title. The title is what shows up in the Related Pages section of every
  other page that links to yours, so treat a change to it as a small
  cross-folder change: search the folder for the old title before you
  commit the new one, since links point to titles as much as to file
  paths. A quick way to find stale references is a plain text search
  across the folder for the exact old title string.

  Version. Bump the version whenever the body of the page changes in a
  way a returning reader would want to know about — a new required field,
  a changed procedure, a corrected example. Do not bump the version for
  whitespace or spelling fixes; note those only in the change log if you
  keep one on the page, or skip them entirely for very small fixes. There
  is ongoing disagreement in the folder about whether the version should
  be a bare decimal or a three-part semantic version; both schemes are in
  live use as of this writing and this page does not attempt to settle it.

  Owner. One team and one named person, always. Do not list two teams in
  the owner field — use section_owners for that instead, described above.
  When ownership moves from one person to another, update the owner field
  on the same day you hand off the page, not on the day the handoff was
  discussed. A page whose owner field names someone who has moved to a
  different team should be treated as stale even if the page's content is
  still accurate.

  Last-updated date. This date is the one the review cadence process
  reads to decide whether a page is due for another look — see
  review-cadence.md for the schedule itself. Set it only when you change
  the page's content, not when you open it to read, and not when an
  automated pass reformats spacing or fixes a broken link without
  touching the meaning of the text.

  Summary. Keep it to one or two sentences. A summary that runs to a full
  paragraph is a sign the page is trying to cover more than one topic and
  might be a candidate for splitting — raise that with the page's owner
  rather than just trimming the summary to fit.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Voice and Front Matter
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section owner: Docs Program (Kara Voss)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
voice_and_front_matter: |
  The header block is the one part of a page where terse, fragment-style
  writing is expected rather than the fuller sentences voice-and-tone.md
  asks for in the body. Field values should read like labels, not like
  sentences: "Specifies the required front matter fields..." rather than
  "This page specifies the required front matter fields...". The Voice
  and Tone Guide covers body prose in detail; this schema only asks that
  summary fields stay short enough to fit on one line in a folder
  listing, roughly 20 words or fewer.

  Capitalization of field labels in a rendered header is not strictly
  fixed across the folder — some pages show "Last Updated," others "Last
  updated," and a couple of older pages still show "Updated." Pick one
  form per page and hold it for every field on that page; do not mix
  "Owner" and "owner" in the same header block.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Page Template Integration
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section owner: Docs Program (Kara Voss)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
page_template_integration: |
  page-templates.md, currently at version 1.3, ships one starter file for
  each of the three page shapes used in this folder — a short reference
  page, a longer procedure page, and a worksheet-style page — and every
  one of those starters already has the five required fields filled in
  with stand-in-shaped values (a bracketed title, a bracketed owner,
  and so on) so a writer only has to replace them, not remember which
  fields exist.

  When this schema changes — for example, the 1.4 update below that adds
  the related-pages and tools-table requirements to every page, not just
  procedure pages — the templates need a matching update so new pages
  don't get created against a stale shape. That update is tracked as a
  small, separate item on page-templates.md's own change log, not on this
  one.

  A minimal starter header, copied from the reference-page template,
  looks like this before anyone fills it in:

  ---
  title: [Page Title]
  version: 1.0
  owner: [Team Name] ([Person Name])
  last_updated: [YYYY-MM-DD]
  summary: >
    [One to two sentences describing what this page covers.]
  ---

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Glossary Upkeep
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
glossary_upkeep: |
  Every page's terminology section, described further under Terminology
  below, is expected to define terms in a way that does not contradict
  terminology-glossary.md, the folder's shared glossary. Front matter
  itself does not carry glossary entries directly, but the summary field
  is the one place a term from the glossary is most likely to appear in a
  sentence a reader sees before opening the page, so it is worth checking
  new or changed summaries against the glossary during a page's review.

  The upkeep procedure is short:

  1. When a page's terminology section adds a term the shared glossary
     does not yet have, open a short entry in terminology-glossary.md in
     the same change, rather than leaving the term defined only on the
     one page that introduced it.
  2. When a page's terminology section defines an existing glossary term
     differently than the glossary does, fix the page to match the
     glossary rather than the other way round — the glossary is the
     source every other page is expected to agree with.
  3. Once a quarter, someone from Platform Tools skims every terminology
     section in the folder against the glossary and flags drift. The
     glossary itself was last rebuilt in a pass that finished in April
     2026, and the schema page you're reading now was checked against
     that pass.

  glossary-terms.txt is a separate, older worksheet kept for draft terms
  that have not yet been promoted into terminology-glossary.md proper —
  treat anything listed there as unsettled, not as a page you can cite.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Review Cadence Integration
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section owner: Docs Program (Kara Voss)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
review_cadence_integration: |
  The last-updated field is the single piece of front matter the review
  cadence process depends on most directly: review-cadence.md sorts every
  page in the folder by that date and flags anything older than the
  window set for its page type. A page whose owner field names someone no
  longer on the relevant team is flagged the same way, even if the date
  itself is recent, since a stale owner usually means the review didn't
  actually happen even though someone bumped the date.

  Because of that, do not "update" the last-updated date on a page
  without also making a real content change — a date-only bump defeats
  the purpose of the cadence check and hides pages that genuinely need a
  look. If a review confirms a page is still accurate with no changes
  needed, note that in the page's own change log (see below) as a
  no-change entry rather than editing the date on its own.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Docs Publishing Workflow Integration
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
publishing_workflow_integration: |
  publishing-workflow.md describes the full path from a merged change to
  a published page; the piece that belongs on this page is the one step
  where front matter is checked before anything else runs. A short shell
  script under scripts/ reads every file changed in a commit, confirms
  the five required fields are present and non-empty, and fails the
  commit hook if any are missing. It does not check field values for
  correctness beyond that — a version of "banana" would still pass — it
  only confirms the fields exist.

  A typical local run, checking a single changed file before pushing,
  looks like this:

  $ scripts/check-front-matter.sh docs/docs-style/front-matter-schema.yaml
  OK: title, version, owner, last_updated, summary all present

  And a pre-commit hook that runs the same check across every staged
  Markdown, RST, and YAML file under docs/docs-style/ before allowing a
  commit:

  #!/usr/bin/env sh
  # .git/hooks/pre-commit
  changed=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM -- 'docs/docs-style/*.md' 'docs/docs-style/*.rst' 'docs/docs-style/*.yaml')
  for f in $changed; do
    scripts/check-front-matter.sh "$f" || exit 1
  done

  A grep-based spot check, useful when the shell script isn't handy, just
  confirms the field labels are present somewhere near the top of a file:

  $ head -n 12 docs/docs-style/front-matter-schema.yaml | grep -E 'title|version|owner|last_updated|summary'

  On Windows, the equivalent using PowerShell's Select-String is:

  PS> Get-Content docs\docs-style\front-matter-schema.yaml -TotalCount 12 | Select-String 'title|version|owner|last_updated|summary'

  Publishing itself is out of coverage for this page — see
  publishing-workflow.md for how a passing check turns into a page on the
  published site.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Worked Examples
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
worked_examples: |
  A complete, valid header for a new procedure page:

  ---
  title: Glossary Upkeep Checklist
  version: 1.0
  owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)
  last_updated: 2026-06-01
  summary: >
    Walks through the quarterly pass that checks page terminology
    sections against the shared glossary.
  ---

  A header with three common problems, shown as it might actually get
  submitted:

  ---
  Title: Glossary Upkeep Checklist
  version: v1
  last_updated: June 1st, 2026
  Summary: A checklist.
  ---

  The problems, in the order a reviewer would flag them:

  - The owner field is missing entirely — the check script would fail
    the commit on this one alone.
  - last_updated is not in ISO 8601 form; "June 1st, 2026" does not sort
    correctly against the rest of the folder and the cadence process
    cannot parse it.
  - The summary is too short to be useful in a folder listing, and field
    capitalization ("Title", "Summary") is inconsistent with the rest of
    the header ("version", "last_updated").

  The fix keeps the same content but corrects the shape:

  ---
  title: Glossary Upkeep Checklist
  version: 1.0
  owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)
  last_updated: 2026-06-01
  summary: >
    Walks through the quarterly pass that checks page terminology
    sections against the shared glossary.
  ---

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Validation Procedure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
validation_procedure:
  - step: 1
    action: >
      Before opening a pull request that touches a docs-style page, run
      scripts/check-front-matter.sh against every file you changed. Fix
      any missing-field failures first — everything downstream assumes
      the five required fields are there.
  - step: 2
    action: >
      Confirm the title field matches, character for character, any
      place another page's Related Pages section already links to this
      one. A quick way is a plain text search for the old title across
      docs/docs-style/ before renaming.
  - step: 3
    action: >
      Confirm the last_updated date is today's date if, and only if, the
      body content changed. Leave it alone for a pure formatting pass.
  - step: 4
    action: >
      Confirm the owner field still names the current owner for the
      page. If ownership changed as part of this edit, say so in the
      change log entry you add.
  - step: 5
    action: >
      Read the summary aloud. If it takes more than one breath to say,
      shorten it.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Files and Paths Referenced by This Page
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
referenced_files:
  - path: docs/docs-style/front-matter-schema.yaml
    function: This page — the schema itself, and the source of truth for required header fields.
  - path: docs/docs-style/README.md
    function: Folder-level overview listing every page in docs-style and a one-line note on each.
  - path: docs/docs-style/voice-and-tone.md
    function: Sentence-level and paragraph-level writing guidance for page bodies.
  - path: docs/docs-style/terminology-glossary.md
    function: The shared glossary that per-page terminology sections must not contradict.
  - path: docs/docs-style/page-templates.md
    function: Starter files for each page shape, pre-filled with the required header fields.
  - path: docs/docs-style/review-cadence.md
    function: The schedule and thresholds used to flag pages whose last-updated date has gone stale.
  - path: docs/docs-style/publishing-workflow.md
    function: The full path from a merged change to a page on the published site, including the front matter check step.
  - path: docs/docs-style/markdown-conventions.md
    function: Heading levels, link style, and list conventions for Markdown pages.
  - path: docs/docs-style/code-block-standards.md
    function: Formatting rules for command and configuration snippets like the ones in section 8 above.
  - path: docs/docs-style/screenshots-and-diagrams.md
    function: Sizing and captioning rules for images embedded in a page body.
  - path: docs/docs-style/changelog-notes.rst
    function: The expected shape of a per-page change log entry, referenced by section 12 below.
  - path: docs/docs-style/style-checklist.rst
    function: A short pre-submit checklist that includes a front-matter line item pointing back to this page.
  - path: docs/docs-style/glossary-terms.txt
    function: A draft worksheet for terms not yet promoted into terminology-glossary.md.
  - path: docs/docs-style/contributor-onboarding.txt
    function: Notes for a new contributor's first week, including where to find this schema.
  - path: scripts/check-front-matter.sh
    function: The shell script that confirms required header fields are present before a commit is allowed.
  - path: .git/hooks/pre-commit
    function: Local hook wiring the check script into every commit that touches docs/docs-style/.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Tools and Libraries
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
tools:
  - name: Python
    version: "3.11.6"
    function: Runtime used by scripts/check-front-matter.sh to parse header fields.
  - name: PyYAML
    version: "6.0.1"
    function: Parses YAML front matter blocks, including this file, during checks.
  - name: yamllint
    version: "1.35.1"
    function: Lints this file and other pure-YAML pages for formatting problems.
  - name: markdownlint-cli
    version: "0.41.0"
    function: Lints Markdown pages after the front matter check passes.
  - name: docutils
    version: "0.20.1"
    function: Parses the two reStructuredText siblings for their header fields.
  - name: git
    version: "2.44.0"
    function: Version control and the host for the local pre-commit hook.
  - name: Pandoc
    version: "3.1.11"
    function: Converts pages into the published site as part of the docs publishing workflow.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. Terminology
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
terminology:
  - term: front matter
    definition: >
      The block of required and optional fields at the top of a
      documentation file — title, version, owner, last-updated date, and
      summary at minimum.
  - term: header block
    definition: >
      Another name for front matter, used interchangeably on most pages
      in this folder; a few older pages call it a "page header" instead.
  - term: required field
    definition: >
      One of the five fields every page must carry: title, version,
      owner, last_updated, and summary.
  - term: optional field
    definition: >
      A field such as status, section_owners, or tags that a page may
      carry but is not checked by scripts/check-front-matter.sh.
  - term: section owner
    definition: >
      A person named against one heading within a page, used on longer
      pages where a single page-level owner does not cover every part.
  - term: sibling page
    definition: >
      Any other page inside docs/docs-style/; used in Related Pages
      sections to mean "a page in this same folder," not a page anywhere
      else in the documentation set.
  - term: stale page
    definition: >
      A page flagged by review-cadence.md because its last-updated date
      has passed the threshold set for its page type, or because its
      owner field names someone no longer on the relevant team.
  - term: schema
    definition: >
      The set of field names, types, and requirements this page defines;
      not a database structure, and unrelated to how the package stores
      its own records.
  - term: check script
    definition: >
      Short name used throughout the folder for
      scripts/check-front-matter.sh, the shell script that confirms
      required fields are present before a commit is allowed.
  - term: no-change entry
    definition: >
      A change log line added after a review confirms a page is still
      accurate, used instead of bumping the last-updated date with no
      real content change behind it.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 14. Change Log
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
changelog:
  - date: 2024-05-02
    release: "1.0"
    change: >
      Initial schema drafted with four required fields: title, owner,
      last-updated date, and summary.
  - date: 2024-11-14
    release: "1.1"
    change: >
      Added version as a fifth required field, aligning the schema with

  - date: 2025-03-06
    release: "1.2"
    change: >
      Clarified the owner field's "team then name" pattern and added a

  - date: 2025-08-22
    release: "1.3"
    change: >
      Added the referenced-files requirement and cross-referenced

  - date: 2026-01-30
    release: "1.3.1"
    change: >
      Fixed inconsistent capitalization of the last-updated field name

  - date: 2026-04-01
    release: "1.4"
    change: >
      Added the related-pages and tools-table requirements to every
      page, not only procedure pages, and expanded the terminology
      section to ten terms.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 15. Related Pages
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
